stem: An engineer tells a client that a retaining wall design is unsafe. The client overrules the engineer and orders construction to proceed as drawn. Under the NCEES Model Rules, what must the engineer do?

options.text: Proceed, because the client carries the liability once informed
Notify the client and any other authority that may be appropriate
Quietly strengthen the design without telling the client
Resign from the project and say nothing further

eli5: Under the Model Rules the first duty is to the health, safety and welfare of the public, ahead of the duty to an employer or client. When professional judgement is overruled and the public is endangered, the engineer must notify the employer or client and any other authority that may be appropriate.
solution:
The first duty in the Model Rules is to the public. When an engineer's judgment is overruled in a way that endangers health, safety or welfare, the engineer must notify the client or employer and any other authority that may be appropriate.

Proceeding, working around the client in secret, or walking away silently all leave the hazard in place.

verify.basis: FE Reference Handbook 10.0.1, Ethics and Professional Practice, Model Rules of Professional Conduct: obligation to the public

stem: During construction an engineer learns that a contractor has left out reinforcement that the drawings require in a public walkway. The engineer's employer says to let it go to stay on schedule. Under the NCEES Model Rules, what must the engineer do?

options.text: Notify the employer and any other authority that may be appropriate
Accept the decision, because the employer directs the work
Wait to see whether the walkway shows distress
Raise the issue anonymously online

eli5: Under the Model Rules the first duty is to the health, safety and welfare of the public, ahead of the duty to an employer or client. When professional judgement is overruled and the public is endangered, the engineer must notify the employer or client and any other authority that may be appropriate.
solution:
The omission endangers the public and the engineer's judgement has been overruled, so the rule on notification applies: tell the employer formally and, if the hazard remains, the authority that can act on it.

Accepting the decision or waiting leaves the hazard in place. An anonymous post is not notification to an appropriate authority.

verify.basis: FE Reference Handbook 10.0.1, Ethics and Professional Practice, Model Rules of Professional Conduct: obligation to the public

stem: A licensed engineer is asked to sign and seal drawings that were produced by another firm. She did not supervise or review the work. May she seal them?

options.text: Yes, if she is licensed in that state
Yes, if the other firm indemnifies her
No, because the work was not prepared under her responsible charge
No, unless the client approves in writing

eli5: A licensee may sign and seal only work prepared under their responsible charge, meaning direct control and personal supervision, and only within their competence. The seal certifies that supervision; it is not a quality stamp added afterwards.
solution:
The Model Rules allow a licensee to seal only work in their area of competence that was prepared under their responsible charge, meaning their direct control and personal supervision.

Being licensed in the state, being indemnified or having the client's approval does not change who was in charge of the work.

verify.basis: FE Reference Handbook 10.0.1, Ethics and Professional Practice, Model Rules of Professional Conduct: signing and sealing; Model Law definition of responsible charge

stem: A colleague who is not licensed completes a drainage design in another office, without a licensed engineer's involvement, and asks her to seal it so it can be submitted today. What should she do?

options.text: Seal it, because the colleague is competent
Seal it after checking the title sheet
Decline, because the work was not prepared under her responsible charge
Let the colleague apply her seal

eli5: A licensee may sign and seal only work prepared under their responsible charge, meaning direct control and personal supervision, and only within their competence. The seal certifies that supervision; it is not a quality stamp added afterwards.
solution:
She had no control over or supervision of the design, so sealing it would violate the Model Rules even if the design is correct.

To seal it properly she would need to take responsible charge: review the work thoroughly, direct any changes and take professional responsibility for it. Letting someone else apply her seal is also a violation.

verify.basis: FE Reference Handbook 10.0.1, Ethics and Professional Practice, Model Rules of Professional Conduct: signing and sealing; Model Law definition of responsible charge

stem: An engineer designing a pump station for a city is offered a paid consulting role by the pump supplier on the same project. When may the engineer accept both payments?

options.text: Never
When the supplier's fee is below a set dollar limit
When the circumstances are fully disclosed and all interested parties agree in writing
When the engineer judges that it will not affect the design

eli5: Licensees must disclose to their employer or client every known or potential conflict of interest, or any circumstance that could influence, or appear to influence, their judgement. Disclosure comes before the decision, and the client decides how to proceed.
solution:
The Model Rules bar compensation from more than one party for services on the same project unless the circumstances are fully disclosed and agreed to in writing by all interested parties.

The engineer's own belief that the design will not be affected is not enough, and there is no dollar threshold.

verify.basis: FE Reference Handbook 10.0.1, Ethics and Professional Practice, Model Rules of Professional Conduct: obligation to employers and clients

stem: An engineer reviewing bids for a city owns shares in one of the bidding contractors. What do the Model Rules require?

options.text: Nothing, provided the review is fair
Disclosure of the conflict of interest to the employer or client
Sale of the shares after the award
A lower score for that bidder to offset any bias

eli5: Licensees must disclose to their employer or client every known or potential conflict of interest, or any circumstance that could influence, or appear to influence, their judgement. Disclosure comes before the decision, and the client decides how to proceed.
solution:
Owning shares in a bidder could influence the review or appear to. The rule is disclosure to the city, which can then reassign the review.

Staying silent, selling later or adjusting scores all leave the client uninformed.

verify.basis: FE Reference Handbook 10.0.1, Ethics and Professional Practice, Model Rules of Professional Conduct: obligation to employers and clients

stem: A professional engineer licensed in one state wants to offer engineering services in a second state. Which route does the NCEES Model Law provide for someone who already holds a license elsewhere?

options.text: Practice under the home-state license for up to one year
Licensure by comity
Retake the FE exam
Register as an engineer intern

eli5: Engineering licences are issued by each state or territory and are valid only there. Practising or offering to practise elsewhere requires that jurisdiction's licence, usually obtained through comity on the strength of the existing licence, exams and experience.
solution:
Licensure by comity lets a board license an engineer who holds a license from another jurisdiction with comparable requirements.

A home-state license does not carry over on its own, and the FE exam and intern status are steps before a first license.

verify.basis: FE Reference Handbook 10.0.1, Ethics and Professional Practice, Model Law: licensure by comity

stem: An engineer licensed only in State A is asked to seal drawings for a project in State B. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The State A seal is valid in every state
The seal is valid if the client is based in State A
Passing the FE exam allows practice in any state
The engineer must first be licensed in State B

eli5: Engineering licences are issued by each state or territory and are valid only there. Practising or offering to practise elsewhere requires that jurisdiction's licence, usually obtained through comity on the strength of the existing licence, exams and experience.
solution:
The project is in State B, so State B's licensing law applies. The engineer must obtain a State B licence, normally by comity, before sealing the drawings.

Where the client is based does not matter, and the FE exam alone grants no right to practise.

verify.basis: FE Reference Handbook 10.0.1, Ethics and Professional Practice, Model Law: licensure by comity

stem: In a negligence claim, an engineer's work is judged against which standard?

options.text: A guarantee that the finished work is free of defects
The care and skill ordinarily used by competent engineers in similar circumstances
Whatever the client instructed
The lowest-cost design that meets code

eli5: Negligence requires a duty, a breach of the standard of care, causation and damages. The standard of care is the skill and care ordinarily exercised by reasonably prudent engineers doing similar work in similar circumstances. It does not promise a perfect outcome.
solution:
The standard of care is what a reasonably prudent engineer would do in the same situation.

It is not a warranty of a perfect result, and following a client's instruction does not excuse careless work.

verify.basis: Common-law principle of professional negligence (standard of care for design professionals)

stem: A design followed the practice that reasonably prudent engineers would have used at the time, yet the structure later performed poorly. In a negligence claim, what is the most likely finding on the standard of care?

options.text: It was breached, because the outcome was poor
It was not breached, because the standard is reasonable care, not perfection
It was breached, because engineers guarantee results
It does not apply to engineers

eli5: Negligence requires a duty, a breach of the standard of care, causation and damages. The standard of care is the skill and care ordinarily exercised by reasonably prudent engineers doing similar work in similar circumstances. It does not promise a perfect outcome.
solution:
The engineer did what a reasonably prudent engineer would have done, so the standard of care was met and there is no breach, whatever the outcome.

Engineers do not guarantee results unless a contract says so.

verify.basis: Common-law principle of professional negligence (standard of care for design professionals)

stem: Which type of insurance covers claims that an engineer's design errors caused a client financial loss?

options.text: General liability
Professional liability (errors and omissions)
Workers' compensation
Builder's risk

eli5: Each policy covers a different risk. Professional liability (errors and omissions) covers losses from design errors. General liability covers injury or property damage to others from operations. Workers' compensation covers a firm's own employees who are hurt at work. Builder's risk covers the structure under construction.
solution:
Professional liability insurance covers negligent acts, errors and omissions in professional services.

General liability covers bodily injury and property damage, workers' compensation covers employee injuries, and builder's risk covers the work while it is being built.

verify.basis: Standard insurance definitions used in construction and design contracts

stem: An employee of an engineering firm is injured while inspecting a construction site. Which insurance pays the employee's medical costs and lost wages?

options.text: Professional liability insurance
Builder's risk insurance
Workers' compensation insurance
A performance bond

eli5: Each policy covers a different risk. Professional liability (errors and omissions) covers losses from design errors. General liability covers injury or property damage to others from operations. Workers' compensation covers a firm's own employees who are hurt at work. Builder's risk covers the structure under construction.
solution:
The injured person is the firm's own employee, hurt in the course of work, so workers' compensation responds.

Professional liability answers claims about the design, builder's risk covers the work itself, and a bond is a guarantee of performance, not insurance for injuries.

verify.basis: Standard insurance definitions used in construction and design contracts

stem: Which of the following is required for a contract to be enforceable?

options.text: Notarization of all signatures
Consideration exchanged by the parties
Approval by the state licensing board
A written document in every case

eli5: An enforceable contract needs an offer, acceptance, consideration, competent parties and a lawful purpose. Consideration is the exchange of something of value by each side; a one-sided promise is a gift, not a contract.
solution:
A valid contract needs an offer, acceptance, consideration, competent parties and a lawful purpose.

Many contracts are enforceable without being written or notarized.

verify.basis: Common-law elements of a valid contract

stem: A contractor promises to regrade a client's yard, and the client promises nothing in return. Which element of an enforceable contract is missing?

options.text: Offer
Competent parties
Lawful purpose
Consideration

eli5: An enforceable contract needs an offer, acceptance, consideration, competent parties and a lawful purpose. Consideration is the exchange of something of value by each side; a one-sided promise is a gift, not a contract.
solution:
The contractor gives a promise of work but receives nothing, so there is no consideration and the promise cannot be enforced as a contract.

The other elements are present: there is an offer, the parties are competent and regrading is lawful.

verify.basis: Common-law elements of a valid contract

stem: An owner agrees to pay a contractor one fixed price for the whole job, whatever it actually costs the contractor. What type of contract is this?

options.text: Unit price
Cost plus fixed fee
Lump sum
Time and materials

eli5: The payment terms of a contract decide who carries cost risk. Under a lump sum the contractor does, because the price is fixed. Under cost plus a fee the owner does, because actual costs are reimbursed. Unit price contracts split it: the contractor carries the unit cost, the owner the quantity.
solution:
A lump sum contract fixes the total price, so the contractor carries the cost risk.

Unit price pays per measured quantity. Cost plus and time and materials reimburse actual costs.

stem: An owner agrees to reimburse a contractor's actual costs and to pay a fixed fee on top. Which party carries most of the risk of cost overruns?

options.text: The owner
The contractor
The engineer
The surety

eli5: The payment terms of a contract decide who carries cost risk. Under a lump sum the contractor does, because the price is fixed. Under cost plus a fee the owner does, because actual costs are reimbursed. Unit price contracts split it: the contractor carries the unit cost, the owner the quantity.
solution:
Costs are reimbursed whatever they turn out to be, so an overrun is paid by the owner. The contractor's fee is fixed and is not at risk.

Under a lump sum contract the answer would be the contractor.

stem: A supplier offers an engineer a paid holiday if the engineer specifies the supplier's pumps on a client's project. Under the NCEES Model Rules, what should the engineer do?

options.text: Accept, provided the pumps meet the specification
Accept, then tell the client afterwards
Decline the offer
Accept only if the value is modest

eli5: Licensees shall not solicit or accept gratuities, directly or indirectly, from contractors, their agents or other parties in connection with work for employers or clients. No favour needs to be requested; the gift itself compromises independence or appears to.
solution:
The Model Rules forbid soliciting or accepting gratuities from contractors, suppliers or other parties in connection with work for an employer or client.

The quality of the product does not change that.

verify.basis: FE Reference Handbook 10.0.1, Ethics and Professional Practice, Model Rules of Professional Conduct: obligation to employers and clients

stem: A contractor working on an engineer's project offers the engineer free use of a holiday home, with no request attached. What should the engineer do?

options.text: Accept, because nothing was asked in return
Accept, and disclose it after the project closes
Decline, because gratuities from contractors in connection with the work are not allowed
Accept only if colleagues can use it too

eli5: Licensees shall not solicit or accept gratuities, directly or indirectly, from contractors, their agents or other parties in connection with work for employers or clients. No favour needs to be requested; the gift itself compromises independence or appears to.
solution:
The offer comes from a contractor on the engineer's own project, so it is a gratuity in connection with the work and must be declined.

Disclosing later or sharing it does not cure the problem.

verify.basis: FE Reference Handbook 10.0.1, Ethics and Professional Practice, Model Rules of Professional Conduct: obligation to employers and clients
